Hi Aisha — thanks for the logs. I skimmed the repro payload and a few red flags:

1) Combined embed + reranker in a single synchronous request: your payload shows you first request embeddings for 200 docs then immediately call the reranker in the same job without KV caching between calls. This can produce short bursts of CPU/RAM pressure.
2) Large per-document context: several items have >8k characters (we truncate at inference time but upstream memory can spike).
3) No batching backoff/retries for 5xx: I don’t see a jittered exponential backoff.

Quick suggestions to try before the call:
- Reduce batch to 50 and pipeline: 1) request embeddings in batches, 2) persist vectors to your DB, 3) call reranker in smaller groups with cached embeddings.
- Add jittered exponential backoff for 502/503 (max attempts 5, base 500ms).
- Increase request timeout to 180s only for reranker calls that may hit longer latencies.
- If you’re using our Python SDK, use the streaming client variant for long responses and set stream=True to avoid client-side timeouts. I’ve pasted a short SDK snippet in the attachment (redwood-sdk-snippet.txt).

I’ll also ask infra to surface server-side traces for your API key between 2026-03-27T15:30 and 2026-03-27T18:30.

—Dev

Morning — quick update from infra after looking at the traces for Finlytics' key. We see a pattern: 

- Timeslice 2026-03-27T15:45–16:15Z: elevated 502s originating from the batch worker pool (cpu saturation) on a few nodes.
- Payloads that triggered failures had a combination of: >150 items + some documents with >6k char contexts + synchronous rerank calls.
- Server side logs show occasional OOM warnings right before a 502 for the batch-worker container.

Immediate mitigation we can enable from our side (no deploy required):
- Temporary per-key concurrency cap to limit parallel batch jobs to 4.
- Enable request size gating for your key to reject >200MB requests with a clearer 413 so you can handle it client-side.

If you’re able to implement the client changes Dev suggested, that should remove the pressure. We can flip the temp concurrency cap off after a week of stable runs.

Let me know if you want us to enable the two mitigations now — we can do that during or immediately after the sync.

—Dylan
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.khan@finlytics.com>

Thanks everyone — we ran the two 50-item tests before the call and both succeeded with no 5xx. The full pipeline with 150+ items still produced occasional 502s yesterday; we’ll implement Dev’s backoff + smaller batches this week.

Please go ahead and enable the temporary per-key concurrency cap and the request size gating; keeping the more informative 413 will help our retry logic.

Appreciate the quick turnaround. I’ll update the ticket in HubSpot after we validate this week.

—Aisha
